subject: English Language
title: Adjectives
introduction: Learn adjective kinds and degrees of comparison, then answer five questions at a time.

rules.title: What an adjective does
rules.body: An adjective describes or limits a noun. It can come before a noun or after a linking verb such as is, seems or tastes. An adverb describes a verb.
rules.example: a narrow lane · The lane is narrow. · The tea tastes sweet.

rules.title: Kinds of adjectives
rules.body: Quality describes what something is like; number tells how many or which in order; quantity tells how much. Demonstrative points out, interrogative asks, and possessive shows ownership.
rules.example: vast syllabus · third row · much courage · these bats · which book · their country

rules.title: Degrees of comparison
rules.body: Use the positive form without comparison, the comparative for two, and the superlative for a group. Short adjectives often add -er/-est; longer ones use more/most.
rules.example: large · larger · largest; beautiful · more beautiful · most beautiful

rules.title: Irregular forms and common traps
rules.body: Good becomes better/best; bad becomes worse/worst. Do not combine more with -er or most with -est. Use fewer for countable things and less for amounts.
rules.example: better answer · the best answer · fewer books · less water

worked.prompt: Of all the players on the team, Vikram is the _____ runner. (fast)
worked.explanation: Of all compares Vikram with the whole team, so use the superlative.

questions.prompt: The blue whale is _____ than the elephant. (large)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: This is the _____ painting in the art exhibition. (beautiful)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: My new school bag is _____ than my old one. (light)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: Of all the players on the team, Vikram is the _____ runner. (fast)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: Today's weather is _____ than yesterday's. (pleasant)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: This road is _____ than the one we took yesterday. (narrow)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: Mount Everest is one of the _____ mountains in the world. (high)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: The second chapter of the book was _____ than the first one. (exciting)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: This is the _____ meal I have ever tasted. (good)
questions.explanation: Use the degree of comparison that fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: 9. Which of the following sentences uses degree of comparison incorrectly?

options.text: (a) This is the most quickest way home.
(b) This is the best solution ever proposed.
(c) He seems cleverer than his brother.

questions.explanation: Most quickest wrongly combines two superlative forms.

questions.prompt: 10. Many buildings surround the park. In this sentence, ‘many’ is an adjective of:
questions.explanation: Many counts buildings; in this school classification it is an adjective of number.

questions.prompt:
12. _______ apples are fresh and ripe. Fill in the blank with a demonstrative
    adjective.
questions.explanation: These points to plural apples.

questions.prompt: (a) The soldiers fought to protect their country.
questions.explanation: their — possessive names the adjective and its kind.

questions.prompt: (b) He was seated in the third row.
questions.explanation: third — numeral names the adjective and its kind.

questions.prompt: (c) The history syllabus is vast.
questions.explanation: vast — quality names the adjective and its kind.

questions.prompt: (d) These cricket bats are for sale.
questions.explanation: These — demonstrative names the adjective and its kind.

questions.prompt: (e) Which book has been awarded the prize?
questions.explanation: Which — interrogative names the adjective and its kind.

questions.prompt: (a) The final exam turned out to be ______ than the mid term. (challenging)
questions.explanation: Choose the positive, comparative or superlative form from the comparison in the sentence.

questions.prompt: (b) This is the ______ decision I have ever had to make. (difficult)
questions.explanation: Choose the positive, comparative or superlative form from the comparison in the sentence.

questions.prompt: (c) The novel we read last summer was ______. (engaging)
questions.explanation: Choose the positive, comparative or superlative form from the comparison in the sentence.

questions.prompt: (d) Of all the students, she is the ________. (smart)
questions.explanation: Choose the positive, comparative or superlative form from the comparison in the sentence.

questions.prompt: (e) The weather feels _________ than it felt yesterday. (unpredictable)
questions.explanation: Choose the positive, comparative or superlative form from the comparison in the sentence.

questions.prompt: The tea tastes ___. (sweet)
questions.explanation: After tastes, use an adjective to describe the tea.

questions.prompt: Of the two routes, this one is the ___. (short)
questions.explanation: The comparative is used when comparing two routes.

questions.prompt: Of all the runners, Asha is the ___. (fast)
questions.explanation: Of all calls for the superlative.

questions.prompt: This task is ___ than yesterday’s. (good)
questions.explanation: Better is the irregular comparative of good.

questions.prompt: That was the ___ day of the trip. (bad)
questions.explanation: Worst is the irregular superlative of bad.

questions.prompt: I have ___ books than my brother. (few)
questions.explanation: Use fewer with countable books.

questions.prompt: There is ___ water in this jar than in that one. (little)
questions.explanation: Use less with uncountable water.

questions.prompt: She chose the ___ of the two paintings. (beautiful)
questions.explanation: The comparative describes the better choice of two.

questions.prompt: The puppy seems ___ after its nap. (happy)
questions.explanation: Seems takes an adjective describing the puppy.

questions.prompt: This is the ___ solution we have found so far. (practical)
questions.explanation: The superlative compares all solutions found so far.

questions.prompt: The crimson scarf belongs to Mira. Which adjective of quality describes the scarf?
questions.explanation: Crimson describes the colour of the scarf, so it is an adjective of quality.

questions.prompt: ___ answer is acceptable; you may choose one of the two. (distributive adjective)
questions.explanation: Either singles out one of two alternatives.

questions.prompt: This is ___ pen, not yours. (I)
questions.explanation: My is the possessive adjective before pen.

questions.prompt: I need ___ information before deciding. (far)
questions.explanation: Further can mean additional.

questions.prompt: The ___ chapter is more difficult than the first. (two)
questions.explanation: Second is an ordinal adjective.

questions.prompt: Her explanation was ___ than mine. (clear)
questions.explanation: Clearer is the usual comparative; more clear is also grammatical.

questions.prompt: The Himalayas are among the ___ mountain ranges in the world. (high)
questions.explanation: Among the highest uses a superlative with a plural noun.

questions.prompt: The captain showed ___ courage during the rescue. (much; adjective of quantity)
questions.explanation: Much expresses an amount of uncountable courage.
